topic: Study of pressure distribution over an aerofoil at various angles of attack, determination of center of pressure and aerodynamic center.
syllabus_extract: Study of pressure distribution over an aerofoil at various angles of attack, determination of center of pressure and aerodynamic center. various forces e.g. lift, drag and moments
specific_objectives: 6.1.2.1 Trainee will be able to describe various types of aerofoil sections, conditions of performance, theories, and concept related with performance

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Analysis of pressure distribution graphs for different angles of attack; identification of CP and AC locations; safety: Handle graph sheets carefully; supervision: Instructor monitors graph interpretation.
intro_questions: What are the primary forces acting on an aerofoil?
How does the angle of attack affect lift generation?

summary_questions: Explain why the aerodynamic center remains constant while the center of pressure moves.
Describe how pressure distribution changes as the angle of attack increases towards stall.
How does the location of the center of pressure affect the pitching moment of the aerofoil?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note comparing the NACA series aerofoil characteristics discussed in the next lesson with the general pressure distribution concepts covered today, focusing on how shape influences the center of pressure.

pft_rows.syllabus: NACA series, Vortex theory, Magnus effect, Kutta Jakubowski law, Span wise flow, down Wash wing tip and trailing edge vortices. Methods for preventing span-wise flow.
